title: Revenue Recovery Bulletin: Unpaid Final-Bill Balances on Closed Electric Service Agreements
content:
**Final Accounts Unit, Revenue Recovery: balances left on closed Electric Service Agreements**

Under the Electric Service Agreement, balances follow the customer, not the address. This bulletin states the terms that govern an unpaid final-bill balance left on a closed agreement.

## Terms in force

**Ageing of the final bill.** A transfer is made only when the final bill of the closed agreement has remained unpaid for at least the prior balance transfer period after its due date. The period is counted in calendar days, starting the day after the final bill's due date, and the transfer may be made on the day the count reaches the period, not before. The period that applies is the value set by the closed agreement's own schedule. The test reads the company's bill records for the closed agreement (its final bill and that bill's due date).

**Receiving agreement.** The receiving agreement is the same customer's open agreement (active, notice pending or disconnected) with the earliest start date. When the customer has no open agreement, the balance stays on the closed agreement.

**Credit balances.** A credit balance is never transferred; it is refunded under the company's stop-service and final-bill terms.

## Time test, worked on both sides (hypothetical)

*Hypothetical figures, chosen for illustration only:* a closed agreement whose schedule sets a period of 20 days, and a final bill due on 1 April that remains unpaid.

| Date | Day of the count | Transfer permitted? |
|---|---|---|
| 2 April | day 1 | no |
| 20 April | day 19 (the day before the count reaches the period) | no |
| 21 April | day 20 (the count reaches the period) | yes |
| 22 April | day 21 | yes |

## Receiving agreement (hypothetical)

A customer's open agreements started on 3 March 2021 (active) and on 9 June 2019 (disconnected). The receiving agreement is the one started on 9 June 2019: disconnected status counts as open, and the earliest start date decides.

## Clauses no longer in force

The following clauses of these terms are no longer in force and are superseded by the current basis:

- the clause that an unpaid final-bill balance left on a closed agreement is transferred to an open agreement of the same customer;
- the clause that the transfer posts two entries for the whole unpaid balance of the closed agreement on the same posting date, namely a prior balance transfer program credit on the closed agreement referencing the receiving agreement and a prior balance transfer program debit on the receiving agreement referencing the closed agreement;
- the clause that a transferred balance becomes part of the receiving agreement's next bill cycle and is past due on that agreement only after that bill's due date.

superseded_clauses: An unpaid final-bill balance left on a closed agreement is transferred to an open agreement of the same customer.

The transfer posts two entries for the whole unpaid balance of the closed agreement on the same posting date — a service_program_credit with credit_code prior_balance_transfer on the closed agreement whose source_reference_id is the receiving agreement, and a service_program_debit with charge_code prior_balance_transfer on the receiving agreement whose source_reference_id is the closed agreement.
A transferred balance becomes part of the receiving agreement's next bill cycle and is past due on that agreement only after that bill's due date.
